candidates.title: Automate due-date reminders from a sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Connect a spreadsheet to a workflow that searches rows and sends reminders based on due dates.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to connect Google Sheets to my Make scenario using the Search Rows module so I can automate reminders based on due dates stored in a spreadsheet.

ease.reason: A small mock can use sample rows and due dates, but no attached reference documents the Google Sheets connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small professional-services operator might pay for due-date reminders; the request establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use sample rows and a test reminder, while connection setup and delivery behavior are unsupported here.

autonomy.reason: A scheduled search and reminder are repeatable in the proposed design; a person must check dates, recipients, and failures.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly names Sheets Search Rows and due-date reminders, but gives no implementation or repeat-use evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: concrete request, but no supplied implementation reference supports the connection, and AI adds no evidenced benefit to a conventional reminder workflow.

candidates.title: Review store information buyers may miss

demandEvidence.chore: Review store information such as reviews, policies, contact details, or business background for gaps that might make a buyer hesitate.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Is there any missing information—such as reviews, policies, contact details, or business background—that would make you hesitate to buy?

ease.reason: An operator can supply fictional store text for a checklist, but no implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: an ecommerce merchant might pay for a store-readiness review; this single question does not establish payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can flag absent supplied categories, but cannot establish which omissions deter actual buyers.

autonomy.reason: A draft checklist can be generated from supplied text, while a merchant must verify accuracy and decide what to change.

evidence.reason: The post lists reviews, policies, contact details, and business background as possible concerns, but gives one feedback question only.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a mock checklist is possible, but this exact idea has recent recorded rejections for limited repeat-use evidence and no implementation support.

candidates.title: Capture customer instructions before checkout

demandEvidence.chore: Allow customers to enter special instructions or custom messages before checkout.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to allow customers to add special instructions or custom messages before they proceed to checkout.

ease.reason: A mock cart can capture a fictional message, but no attached reference documents checkout customization.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a store operator might pay for a checkout customization; this request establishes no buyer commitment or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can test message capture, but live checkout integration and order-note persistence are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A configured field could capture text in a proposed mock; a person must verify that notes reach the intended order.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly requests customer instructions or messages before checkout, but gives no implementation details or repeat demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the exact feature has recent recorded rejections; supplied evidence supports a one-off customization request, with no relevant implementation reference or evidenced AI role.
